messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: scale_y_inverse problem
parts:
Using the mpg data, I get the following error:

   qplot(displ, hwy, data=mpg) +  scale_y_inverse()
   Error in to - from : non-numeric argument to binary operator

scale_y_log10 causes no problems.

By the way, I think either inverse (gallons/mile) or log scale is a better way to present the mpg data.

ggplot2 0.8.3
R 2.8.1
Windows XP

messages.author: 969bc1db85a35ba3
messages.subject: Re: scale_y_inverse problem
parts:
have a look at http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/scale_inverse.html

you haven't specified a transformation and the default is NULL.

to get log10 transformation, try

qplot(displ, hwy, data=mpg) + scale_y_inverse(trans="log10")

HTH

Gary

messages.subject: Re: scale_y_inverse problem
parts:
Thanks for the quick reply. Actually, I did look at the man page before posting, and it does not mention that any parameters are required. What's more, the text of the page is identical to the text of the scale_log page (substituting the word 'log' for the word 'inverse/interse' (typo)), and scale_log (as I mentioned) does not require any parameters.

But actually, according to the ggplot book, I should have been using "recip" for multiplicative inverse, not "inverse".  But neither scale_y_continuous(trans="recip") nor scale_y_recip() works.

I am even more confused when I compare scale_y_continuous(trans='log10') and scale_y_inverse(trans='log10'), which appear to do the same thing.

            -s

messages.author: 969bc1db85a35ba3
messages.subject: Re: scale_y_inverse problem
parts:
Apologies, I was a bit quick off the mark. After I'd replied, I
realised what you were asking and I agree. I too followed the same steps
you took and have come to the same conclusion, as you say according to
the book you should be able to call "recip" - it is indeed baffling.

In addition, on the man page for scale_y_continuous, under the examples
there is a note saying see ?transformer for a full list but there is no
man page for this.

as a quick fix, you could try

qplot(displ, 1/hwy, data=mpg)

Gary
